public_rationale: Primary evaluations support recurring failures across multiple model families, especially alignment failures under controlled conditions. They do not verify nearly all seven prediction categories for every subsequent model. Structured outputs also show that a narrower part of the integration problem has improved substantially, without proving dependable general integration. The universal retrospective claim remains broader than the available evidence.
limitations: Representative failures cannot establish a universal claim about all model versions.
Anthropic evaluates its own models as well as competitors.
Simulated failures do not measure their prevalence in ordinary deployments.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Almost all of his December 2022 predictions about GPT-4 remain true, and the same problems plague every model since, including GPT-5, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Llama and DeepSeek.

statement.excerpt: Three years and nearly a trillion dollars later almost of all it remains true. And it’s not just that GPT-4 was pretty much as I anticipated but that the same problems have continued to plague every single model since
statement.document_title: Three years on, ChatGPT still isn't what it was cracked up to be – and it probably never will be

from_speaker: almost of all it remains true
our_interpretation: The supplied normalized proposition concerns persistence of the December 2022 predictions, rather than the incidental investment estimate.

The referenced categories are control and errors; reasoning and medical reliability; hallucinations and safeguards; downstream integration; general-purpose autonomy; alignment; and the eventual role of structured systems in AGI.
The ordinary reading is that nearly all these limitations persisted across subsequent model families. The words 'every single model' are not silently reduced to a few representative models.
The period starts with the December 2022 predictions and ends at publication.
Predictions about how eventual AGI will be built cannot be treated as verified merely because current systems retain limitations.
criteria.support_condition: Public evaluations provide sufficiently comprehensive coverage of subsequent model versions and the concrete prediction categories to establish that nearly all the asserted limitations persisted across the claimed population.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evaluations demonstrate dependable resolution of enough prediction categories to defeat 'almost all', or establish a model that does not share the asserted persistent problems under the same scope and operating conditions.

evidence.explanation: Controlled simulations found harmful behavior in models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, xAI and DeepSeek. This supports persistent alignment problems across families, but covers neither every version nor every prediction, and does not establish real-world incidence.

Constrained decoding provides documented progress on dependable program interfaces. The guarantee concerns schema compliance, not semantic correctness or arbitrary downstream actions, so it does not decisively refute Marcus's broader reliability wording.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated inventory of the models covered and a prediction-by-prediction evaluation using consistent definitions, including tools and operating conditions. The eventual-AGI proposition would need separate treatment.
